extracted.subtask_short: RCE filing and processing for US patents
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards and requirements for filing, processing, and evaluating Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) under 37 C.F.R. 1.114 in U.S. patent prosecution, including what submissions/fees are required, timing constraints, and examiner handling in various prosecution states (after final, allowance, appeal, Board decision, court review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application eligibility for RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: RCE provisions of 37 C.F.R. 1.114 apply to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, and to international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995 that comply with 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice does not apply to provisional applications, utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, international applications before June 8, 1995 or international applications that do not comply with 35 U.S.C. 371, design patent applications, international design applications, or patents under reexamination (see 37 C.F.R. 1.114(e)). For national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, required inventor’s oaths/declarations (or substitute statements) must be submitted prior to or with the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE (submission plus fee) must be filed prior to the earliest of: payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.313 is granted), abandonment of the application, or filing of a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit / commencement of a civil action (unless that appeal/civil action is terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, an RCE cannot be filed until prosecution in the application is closed (i.e., application is under appeal, last Office action is a final action, a notice of allowance, or an action otherwise closing prosecution such as an Ex parte Quayle action). Filing after Board decisions has special timing rules (see section XI). Filing after court review generally not allowed (see XII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and content of a submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' for RCE purposes may include an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the specification/claims/drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 C.F.R. 1.111. An appeal brief or reply brief alone is not a submission, but arguments in a previously filed appeal/reply brief may be incorporated by reference. Previously filed after-final amendments that were not entered may in some cases satisfy the submission requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement and conditional payment
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 C.F.R. 1.17(e). The Director may set fees and provide reduced fees for small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'conditional' RCE with authorization to charge a deposit account is treated as if payment had been made. Failure to pay the RCE fee will generally render the RCE improper; missing fee may cause submission not to be entered (see form paragraphs for handling). Payment of the RCE fee alone does not toll time periods — the submission must meet reply requirements to toll (see VI and V).

rubrics_metrics.name: No switching inventions (independent and distinct claims prohibited)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant cannot obtain continued examination via RCE for claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., cannot 'switch inventions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any newly submitted claims directed to an invention independent and distinct from the previously claimed invention will be withdrawn from consideration and not entered. See 37 C.F.R. 1.145 and subsection VI for examples and treatment of such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing verification by Technology Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel will verify that the application is utility/plant (not design), filed on/after June 8, 1995, prosecution is closed, RCE filed before issue fee (or petition granted), application pending, proper fee(s) paid, submission included, and for national stage apps a compliant oath/declaration was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is undergoing court review at the Federal Circuit or in federal district court, the RCE will not be processed because jurisdiction rests with the court (see subsection XII). The checklist items (A–H) should be used to determine proper processing or issuance of Notice of Improper RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper RCE (notice and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more filing conditions are not satisfied (e.g., missing fee, missing submission, wrong application type, prosecution not closed), the applicant will be notified (generally via Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination, Form PTO-2051) and the RCE will be improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An improper RCE will not toll any running time periods set in the previous Office action; it will not prevent abandonment. If forwarded to examiner in error, return to HSLIE. Specific improper scenarios (prosecution not closed, application under appeal without fee/submission) have prescribed handling and form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal paper handling (CPA vs RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmittal paper ambiguously refers to a CPA (continued prosecution application) and an RCE, for utility/plant applications filed on/after June 8, 1995 the Office will treat it as an RCE; for design applications it will be treated as a CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other papers accompanying the transmittal (e.g., preliminary amendment or IDS) are not considered in deciding whether the transmittal is a CPA or RCE. An unambiguous RCE filed in a design application will be treated as an improper RCE (RCE practice does not apply to design apps). The Office will not convert RCEs into new applications (e.g., CPA or 1.53(b) continuation) except under narrow extenuating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and ordering of amendments on a proper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is proper, previously filed unentered amendments and amendments filed with the RCE will normally be entered in the order filed unless specific entry instructions are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to file all desired amendments no later than filing the RCE to avoid disapproval under 37 C.F.R. 1.111(b). If conflicting previously-filed amendments exist, applicant should clarify which to enter. If additional time is needed to supplement a submission (e.g., affidavit with test data), consider filing a suspension of action under 37 C.F.R. 1.103(c) with the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess/new claims fees when filing an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants do not need to pay a fee for excess claims previously paid prior to filing the RCE; however, new claims in excess of the number previously paid for, filed with or after the RCE, will require payment of appropriate fees under 37 C.F.R. 1.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any claim-count-related fees are addressed at or after RCE filing when adding claims beyond previously-paid numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submissions — bona fide attempt requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a final Office action is outstanding, a submission filed with an RCE must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to that final Office action for the RCE to toll the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that are not bona fide (e.g., only an IDS when a reply to final is outstanding; an amendment cancelling all claims without presenting new/substitute claims) are not fully responsive and will be treated as improper, not tolling the reply period. If the submission is a bona fide attempt but not fully responsive (e.g., non-compliant amendment), applicant should be notified, and given a shortened statutory period (typically two months) to complete/correct the reply (form paragraph 7.42.08). Examples: (A) non-compliant amendment — give two months to correct to comply with 37 C.F.R. 1.121; (B) presentation of claims to a different invention — treat amendment as not entered and give two months to submit a complete reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant amendment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed with an amendment that does not comply with 37 C.F.R. 1.121 but is a bona fide attempt to reply should be treated as a proper RCE; applicant is mailed a Notice of Noncompliant Amendment and given two months to submit a compliant amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.03 for specifics on amendment practice and the mechanics of compliance with 1.121. Use form paragraph 7.42.08 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of claims for a different invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed with an amendment that cancels all claims to the elected invention and presents only claims to a non-elected invention (lack of unity), the RCE is proper but the amendment is not entered as fully responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be given two months to submit a complete reply. Use form paragraphs 8.04 or 8.26 as appropriate. See 37 C.F.R. 1.145 and MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment where submission is entered but not persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments previously submitted after final and entered by the examiner but not found persuasive may still satisfy the RCE submission requirement if they are responsive within the meaning of 37 C.F.R. 1.111 to the outstanding Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of responsiveness is done without factoring the 'final' status of the outstanding action; a reply acceptable under 1.111 may be acceptable for RCE even if it would not be acceptable under 1.113 in a final rejection context.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 132(a) prohibits amendments that introduce new matter; any amendment entered pursuant to 37 C.F.R. 1.114 found to contain new matter must be treated the same as a reply under 1.111 determined to contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant seeks to add new matter, the RCE route is not available; applicant must file a continuation-in-part application under 37 C.F.R. 1.53(b) containing the new matter. See MPEP §§ 608.04–608.04(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office action after RCE may be final only under conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Office action made after filing an RCE (submission + fee) may be made final only if conditions in MPEP § 706.07(b) are met; it is improper to make that first action final if it includes a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final, set a shortened statutory period for reply (e.g., three months), with special advisory-action timing rules if a first reply is filed within two months. Use form paragraph 7.42.09 when appropriate. See MPEP § 1207.03 for discussion on what constitutes a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after allowance or Quayle action — reopening prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE with fee and submission filed in an allowed application (or after Ex parte Quayle action) reopens prosecution and the submission will be entered and considered, provided the issue fee has not already been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the issue fee has been paid, an RCE plus a petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.313 to withdraw from issue is required; if petition is filed and granted prosecution reopens, applicant may not obtain refund of the previously-paid issue fee. Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to notify applicant that prosecution has been reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but before Board decision — effect on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed after filing a Notice of Appeal to the PTAB but prior to a Board decision is treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner, regardless of whether the RCE is proper or improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper (fee + submission responsive under 1.111), withdraw finality and enter submission. If improper (missing fee/submission or not bona fide), the appeal is still withdrawn and the application is treated per MPEP § 1215.01 — e.g., if no claim allowed, application abandoned; if claims allowed, pass to issue or give shortened statutory period to correct formal matters. Use form paragraphs 7.42.06 and 7.42.10–7.42.14 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE after Board decision but before further appeal or civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed after a Board decision but before filing a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencing civil action will withdraw finality of the rejection and reopen prosecution if filed within the 63-day window (and before notice of appeal) and accompanied by fee and submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a Board decision has res judicata effect; a submission consisting only of argument without amendment or a showing of facts will not be effective to remove new grounds of rejection entered by the Board. Use form paragraph 7.42.07 to notify applicant when prosecution reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE after Board decision (missing fee/submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a Board decision but lacks the fee and/or submission, the RCE is improper, any running time periods were not tolled, and the examiner should use form paragraph 7.42.16 to notify applicant (and include with Notice of Allowability/Abandonment or PTOL-90 as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission was filed with such an improper RCE, generally it should not be entered unless the amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance (with supervisory approval). Include a statement whether any submission has been entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE after filing notice of appeal to Federal Circuit or civil action — general bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The RCE procedure under 37 C.F.R. 1.114 is not available after filing a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit or the commencement of a civil action in federal district court, unless that appeal/civil action is terminated and the application remains pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed after court review, the examiner should bring the application to the attention of supervisory personnel or quality assurance to determine whether the RCE is proper. Termination of unsuccessful appeal/civil action generally results in abandonment unless allowed claims or the court’s mandate instructs further Office action (see MPEP § 1216.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required forms and examiner form paragraphs for communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/30 may be used by applicant to file an RCE transmittal; Technology Centers use Form PTO-2051 to notify applicant of an improper RCE. The MPEP identifies numerous standard examiner form paragraphs (e.g., 7.42.04, 7.42.05, 7.42.06, 7.42.08, 7.42.09, 7.42.10–7.42.16) for acknowledging entry, notifying of withdrawal of finality/appeal, setting shortened statutory periods, or indicating improper RCE status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are instructed which form paragraphs to use in particular factual scenarios (e.g., proper RCE after final rejection — 7.42.04; RCE not fully responsive — 7.42.08; continued examination after allowance — 7.42.05; ambiguous CPA treated as RCE — 7.42.15). Applicants should be aware these standard communications will be used to explain examiner actions and deadlines.
